newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: S&P assigns BBB long-term rating to AMMB.
newsitem.headline: S&P assigns BBB long-term rating to AMMB.

text.p: Rating firm Standard and Poor's has assigned a long-term rating of BBB to Arab-Malaysian Merchant Bank Bhd (AMMB), the national Bernama news agency said on Wednesday.
It said quoting a statement from S&P that the merchant bank has been assigned a short-term rating of A3.
The rating reflected AMMB's leading franchise in merchant banking services, strong profitability, adequate risk management systems and good asset quality, S&P said.
It said AMMB's capitalisation, at 6.56 percent in terms of equity-to-assets, was reasonable.
However, AMMB could not get a higher rating because of its high exposure to the property and finance sectors, rapid loan growth and structurally high dependence on wholesale deposits.
"The rating outlook looks stable," S&P was quoted as saying about AMMB, one of the largest merchant banks with assets totalling 14.4 billion ringgit.
